description.narrative: The development objective of the project is to assist PLN to meet growing electricity demand, improve the reliability of electricity supply, strengthen the power transmission system, and support the preparation of hydropower projects.

The objective of the Power Transmission Development Project for Indonesia is to assist the Borrower to meet growing electricity demand and improve the reliability of electricity supply in Java and south-central Sumatra by strengthening the dower transmission system. There are two components to the project, the first component being Java-Bali transmission substation expansion and construction. This component includes: expansion of four existing 500/150 kV and twenty to twenty-five existing 150/20 kV substations through the installation of new transformers and associated equipment; and construction of one new 150/20 kV substation, including two 60 MVA transformers, and installation of associated equipment. Finally, the second component is the South-Central Sumatra transmission substation upgrading and expansion. This component includes: upgrading of five (5) existing 150 kV substations through the installation of new transformers and associated equipment; and expansion of ten (10) to fifteen (15) existing 150/20 kV substations through the transformers and associated equipment.

Transmission losses in the Java-Bali system
Transmission losses in the Java-Bali system

comment.narrative: <p>Transmission losses during 2010 until 2019 period fluctuated. In Java island the highest number of transmission losses was 2.52%in 2012 and decreasing to 2.34% in the end of 2019, against 2.4% targeted. This is around 3% better than expected. The actual losses in Java was better than the target. In Java system, the target and actual losses were higher than the baseline since more electricity was evacuated from East and Central Java to supply the demand in West Java and Jakarta. The actual losses increased above the target due to lengthier distance of transmission line. The project may not fully attribute to this achievement since the project is only part of the bigger power transmission system in Java.</p>

title.narrative: Transmission losses in the Sumatra system
Transmission losses in the Sumatra system

comment.narrative: <p>In Sumatra, the highest number was 3.76% in 2010 and decreasing to 2.64% in the end of 2019 against 2.49% targeted. This is around 6% lower than target. With the main generation at the south and load center at the north part of island, transmitting electricityin long distance along the island will increase the transmission losses.  The actual losses in Sumatra was slightly less than the target. The baseline data was higher than the target and actual losses. The operation of new 275/150 kV transmission line connecting South and Central Sumatra has reduced the transmission losses. However, with recent development of 275/150 kV transmission linestarted to connect North Sumatra as well, the actual losses has increased above the target due to lengthier distance of transmission line. The project may not fully attribute to this achievement since the project is only part of the bigger power transmission system in Java and Sumatra.</p>

title.narrative: Electricity sales in the project areas in south-central Sumatra (GWh)

comment.narrative: <p>The electricity sales in Sumatra increased to 36,294.14 GWh against 34,000.00 GWh targeted. This is around 6.7% better than expected. The target and achievement of annual electricity sales were estimated and measured from the provinces in Sumatra island where the IPTD sub-projects are located. The original target was only covering south - central of Sumatra which then expanded to south - north of Sumatra in the project restructuring. The revised electricity sales targets were increased to adjust the new closing date, from 2015 to 2019, and additional project areas from the sub-projects financed by the project savings. The additional substations capacity has contributed to the increase of customers number and electricity sales, though it could not claim a full attribution to those increases, since external factors beyond the project boundary may have major role. The project partly attributed to this achievement.</p>

comment.narrative: <p>The outcome indicator for this objective is the number of MW hydropower prepared with the completion of two preparatory studies,Feasibility Study (FS) and Environmental & Social Impact Assessment Study (ESIA), as the intermediate indicators. Technical design and preparation of tender documents for Poko Hydroelectric Power Project was completed with the Feasibility Study (FS) and ESIA.The FS is well prepared, and assessments are complete and covering the key technical issues with a recommendation of 124.5 MW for the development of Poko HPP, and additional up to 4.3 MW by a mini hydropower station arranged at the dam toe, with total potential development of 128.8 MW. From a technical perspective the FS is ready to be bid out. However, a lot of thinking on development/implementation aspects, such as tender strategy, contract packaging and most importantly whether to develop it publicly or privately, are still necessary. For private sector involvement, the FS requires further review from technical, legal and transaction advisors with private lender perspective. The Environment and Social Assessments have been completed prepared with the preparation completion of the Poko HPP’s ESIA, Environmental and Social Management Plan (ESMP), and a Cumulative Impact Assessment (CIA), though few works are still required to make those documents fully acceptable by the Bank. The use of MW hydropower capacity as the indicator to assess the achievement of this objective is not the right choice. A prepared hydropower project should be assessed from its readiness to be tendered out with all preparatory documentations, including FS, technical design, tender document, ESIA, LARAP (Land Acquisition and Resettlement Action), should have been completed. Though the objective has been achieved based on the current indicator, Poko HPP could not be considered as prepared and ready with the absence of other preparatory studies.</p>
